historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Melatonin receptor agonists

starting.description: Bovine pineal extract lightened frog tadpole skin; researchers used the observed effect as a bioassay to isolate the responsible endogenous substance, melatonin. Later observations of nighttime melatonin and sleep-related effects helped motivate therapeutic investigation.

inspiration.description: An animal skin-pigment response to pineal extracts led to isolation of the endogenous hormone melatonin; observations of its nighttime rhythm and sleep-related effects informed subsequent therapeutic investigation.

steps.description: An observed frog-skin response to bovine pineal extract supplied a bioassay used to isolate melatonin; the investigators used synthetic material to test its proposed structure.
Pigment-cell pharmacology informed receptor hypotheses and subsequently mammalian receptor cloning.

Observations of nighttime hormone levels and earlier high-dose effects informed a deliberate low-dose human study; an investigator proposed possible use for people with low secretion. Later development included a prolonged-release hormone formulation.

Medicinal chemists prepared hormone-related analogues and replaced its indole core in other agonists; a program synthesized and optimized a constrained indan series, producing the clinical candidate TAK-375.

design.description: Investigators synthesized the identified hormone to test its structure. Later work developed prolonged-release hormone and chemically distinct agonists, including indole-core replacement and conformational restriction to alter receptor-binding and metabolic properties. The complete sequence of predecessors in the indan program is not established by the 2002 abstract.

circumstances.description: The named events are the low-dose oral-melatonin versus placebo physiology experiment and the synthesis of a receptor-active indan series; this does not characterize the chance status of every earlier finding.

limits: The cohort contains melatonin itself: the finding chiefly concerns the endogenous-hormone and replacement branch, not a claim about each brand or formulation.

The indan agonist illustrates a chemically distinct later branch grounded in melatonin-related structure-activity work; its exact intermediate precursor sequence and other companies' individual programs were not reconstructed.
The 1917, 1958 and 1959 originals were located but not read; the source for the historical link is the later receptor review, supplemented by the isolators' 1960 full-text experimental account.
conflicts: The S6 introduction compresses isolation and structure identification into 1958, whereas S2 cites a 1959 structure report; the publisher confirms the existence of the 1959 structure communication S9. Neither the 1958 nor 1959 communication was read, so the exact timing of structural identification is not independently resolved here.
gaps: The original 1917 observation, 1958 isolation communication and 1959 structure communication were located but their experimental texts were not read; their identities and access limits are in the receipt.
The 1994 human experiment was read in an in-press manuscript rather than the final typeset publication; a direct causal link from that study to a particular melatonin product was not established.

The full 2002 medicinal-chemistry paper and its earlier precursor publication were not read; the report was accessed at abstract level and the broad structural relationship is supported by a later review.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: Human sleep investigations and short melatonin exposure supplied a rationale for prolonged-release formulations and longer-lived agonists.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: No unique early trial-to-product bridge is established; efficacy conclusions remain qualified in the source review.
